i6.title: Issue #6: How to Land on a Recruiter's Shortlist Before January
i6.subject: Recruiters are building January's shortlist right now

content.text: Here's something most job seekers don't know: December is when a lot of recruiters quietly build their lists for January. New budgets open, roles get approved, and the first people we call are the ones we already found, or already know. Let's make sure that's you.

Recruiters search LinkedIn by title, skills and location. If your headline still says "Seeking new opportunities," you won't come up. Put the title you want plus two or three search words in your headline (for example "Clinical Research Associate II | Oncology" or "Qualified Professional | I/DD").
2. Turn on Open to Work, privately.
If you're employed, set Open to Work to "Recruiters only" and fill in your target titles, locations and work types. It's one of the filters recruiters use.
3. Make it easy to say yes.
When a recruiter reaches out, reply within a day, even if it's "Not the right fit, but here's what I'm looking for." A clear, quick answer gets you remembered for the next role.

Before the holidays, write down 5 results from this year with numbers (sites monitored, deviations closed, staff hired, census grown). When January calls come, you'll have answers ready instead of scrambling.
Rewrite your LinkedIn headline using the title you want and two search words from a posting you'd love.

One Quick Tip: have your answer ready for "So what are you up to?"

You'll hear it at every holiday gathering this month. Have a one-sentence answer ready: what you do, plus what you're looking for next. For example: "I'm a clinical research associate in oncology, and I'm looking for a CRA II role with less travel." Friends and family can't help with a job search they don't understand, and one clear sentence makes it easy for them to think of you.
